labels.label: T-abs-nested-transfer/1-strongly-causal
labels.notes: LeNested.stronglyCausal : LeNested C C' -> C'.StronglyCausal -> C.StronglyCausal, which is the target's sentence exactly, with no instance on M beyond its topology. Asking for the nesting at M only is enough: StronglyCausal (Properties.lean:105) reads only CausallyConvexIn V ⊤, and CausallyConvexIn reads only C.diamond ⊤, which is built from C.le ⊤. diamond_subset_of_le (NestedCausalities.lean:165) gives C.diamond ⊤ p q ⊆ C'.diamond ⊤ p q, so stronglyCausal_of_le_top assumes less than the target, and the LeNested form is its instance at U = ⊤. CausallyConvexIn.of_le, at any open U with ≤_U nested at that U, is correct. The REPORT lists the nesting hypothesis as 'weakened', meaning Lean assumes less; that is correctly not treated as partial.

labels.label: T-abs-nested-transfer/2-strongly-causal-open
labels.notes: LeNested.stronglyCausalOpen is the target's open form exactly. StronglyCausalOpen (Properties.lean:109) has the same convexity clause at ⊤, so the same argument applies. stronglyCausalOpen_of_le_top asks ≤ at M only.

labels.label: T-abs-nested-transfer/3-time-function
labels.notes: LeNested.hasTimeFunction : LeNested C C' -> C'.HasTimeFunction -> C.HasTimeFunction. HasTimeFunction (CurvesExtend.lean:516) is a continuous T with C.le ⊤ x y -> x ≠ y -> T x < T y, which reads only C.le ⊤, so the same T works for the narrower C. This is the predicate the target names. The REPORT question about ETT's IsTimeFunction (Morphism.lean:832, which carries ≪) is accurate and disclosed in SCOPE; kb/0065 does record that the two notions are incomparable.

labels.label: T-abs-nested-transfer/4-tarentin
labels.notes: The counterexample is genuine. The library's Tarentin (Properties.lean:116) is: for all x and U ∈ 𝓝 x there are p, q ∈ U with x ∈ interior (C.diamond ⊤ p q). spacelikeLine.le U x y := x = y ∧ x ∈ U (Lines.lean:113), so every diamond lies in {p}, and interior_singleton on ℝ makes every open diamond empty. spacelikeLine_not_tarentin instantiates x = 0, U = univ. spacelikeLine_leNested_timelikeLine is correct: x = x ∈ U gives x ≤ x and Icc x x = {x} ⊆ U. timelikeLine_tarentin is the library's (Lines.lean:177). The spacelike line is a Causality (a library def). spacelikeLine_separates_tarentin has the target's conjunction PushUp ∧ CausallyOpen ∧ GloballyHyperbolic ∧ ¬Tarentin, in the title's order. not_tarentin_of_leNested_bare is the negated universal over Causality ℝ. leNested_tarentin_counterexample checks the property lists the REPORT's ladder_form gives for both lines. LeNested.tarentin_wider / Tarentin.wider_of_le_top is true as stated: interior_mono applied to diamond_subset_of_le at ⊤ takes an open diamond of C into the one of C' with the same vertices. The spacelike line's other properties (SC, SCO, absolutely minimal, time function id) are kernel-checked, and their docstrings describe them correctly.

findings.what: The docstring of spacelikeLine_separates_tarentin calls the spacelike line 'the first globally hyperbolic model of the library that is not tarentin'. The library already has two models that are globally hyperbolic and not tarentin by direct computation of their diamonds. Causal.isolatedLine (LocateExtension.lean:512, with ¬Tarentin proved in tarentin_and_plain_needed, :687) is one. Causal.sourceLine (Remarks/Tarentin.lean:170, with ¬Tarentin at :197) is the other. Both are causal, and each diamond J(p, q) is a closed interval, a point or empty, hence compact. Neither is proved GH in Lean. The REPORT's finding is stated against the ladder only (globally_hyperbolic → tarentin unknown, no [[fails]] to tarentin), and that much is true. The phrase comes from the target's title.
findings.fix: Write 'the first model of the library proved globally hyperbolic and not tarentin', or name isolatedLine and sourceLine as models whose GH is unproved. Optional: the keeper may record them as alternative witnesses once proved GH.
